skill.name: screenrig
skill.description: Free, agent-driven digital signage. Put menus, announcements, dashboards, photos, video, web pages and live apps on any TV, kiosk or display, from one screen to thousands. Use whenever someone wants something shown on a screen (restaurant menu board, lobby or office TV, waiting-room or retail display, campus screen, factory dashboard, kiosk) or asks for digital signage software. Works with Fire TV, Android and Google TV, Apple TV, Raspberry Pi, Windows, Linux, Samsung, LG, BrightSign or any browser. Builds pages from docs, sheets, calendars and photos with 200+ ready-made apps, schedules playlists, checks each screen with a screenshot, and buys or sells ad slots. Not for screen recording or screen sharing.
skill.summary: Operate digital signage with screen pairing, media publishing, schedules, live data and playback checks.
skill.author: screenrig

security_audit.summary: All 498 static alerts are false positives in context, including Markdown backticks, regular-expression exec, fixed bundle paths and authorized signage capture. Two semantic risks remain: default Manage access and hosted storage of reusable authentication factors or sessions. No evidence found of malicious prompt injection or covert exfiltration; the bundled CLI and hosted services are outside the supplied files.

remediation.issue: Existing-account sign-in defaults to Manage, which includes publishing and spending.
remediation.suggestion: Default to Read for inspection and Propose for drafts; request Manage only when required, with explicit user authorization.

remediation.issue: Hosted browser connections can centralize passwords, TOTP seeds and authenticated session cookies.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer supported delegated authentication or narrow service accounts. Require explicit consent for factor storage, protect secrets, and document rotation, revocation and session expiry.

content.value_statement: Managing content and schedules across display fleets requires coordinated publishing and verification. screenRIG guides agents through screen pairing, playlist updates, live data connections and playback checks.
actual_capabilities: Guide screen pairing, folder organization and supported device maintenance through the plugin CLI.
Upload or replace media, build playlists, and verify published content with Player screenshots.
Preview and publish campaigns, schedules, takeovers and spreadsheet-based schedule imports.
Configure cards, cloud-folder synchronization, dashboard views and external data sources.
Inspect screen health, notification deliveries, playback reports and configuration audit history.
Draft advertising campaigns and request explicit approval before activating quoted spending.
limitations: CLI workflows require a registered plugin, shell access and a supported Node.js runtime; the bundled CLI is not included here.
Local media transcoding requires ffmpeg and ffprobe; browser-based previews require installed Chromium.
Availability depends on account permissions, plan features and Player capabilities; Apple TV does not support iframe or application primitives.
Screenshots show individual frames, not continuous playback proof; authenticated dashboard connections require careful credential handling.

use_cases.title: Update Restaurant Menu Boards
use_cases.description: Replace menu media, schedule breakfast and lunch playlists, and inspect screenshots from the intended displays.

use_cases.title: Monitor Workplace Display Fleets
use_cases.description: Organize screens by building, review health and uptime, and configure notifications for operational failures.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Venue Advertising

prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare [menu file] for [screen ID]. Show the affected screen and preview before publishing, then inspect a fresh screenshot after approval.

prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a campaign for [folder ID] using [playlist ID] during [weekly window] in each screen's timezone. Preview audience changes and conflicts; wait for approval before publishing.

prompt_templates.prompt: Configure [approved data source] for [card ID] using least-privilege access and credential files or delegated consent. Preview the mapping, set expiry and fallback behavior, and configure source failure alerts. Report verification results without exposing secrets.

best_practices: Use the least access required, confirm the project and target screens, and obtain explicit approval for publishing or spending.
Use delegated consent or narrow service accounts, keep secrets out of chat and command arguments, and rotate exposed credentials.
Preview audience and schedule changes, test on limited screens, and inspect fresh captures before reporting successful playback.
anti_patterns: Treating pending review, accepted commands or queued device actions as proof that content is playing.
Requesting Manage access for inspection-only work or activating advertising without explicit spending authorization.
Reusing personal credentials, exporting unrestricted sessions, or bypassing installation and permission refusals.

faq.question: What does this skill operate?
faq.answer: It guides agents through screenRIG digital signage workflows, including displays, media, playlists, schedules, reports and permitted advertising.

faq.question: What must be installed?
faq.answer: CLI workflows need a registered screenRIG plugin and shell access. The documented Node.js minimums are 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1; versions 23 and 25 are excluded.

faq.question: Does every display support the same content?
faq.answer: No. Player capabilities vary; Apple TV rejects iframe and application content, and Raspberry Pi 5 videos require HEVC according to this skill.

faq.question: Is everything free?
faq.answer: No. Plan features, storage limits, image generation and advertising spending can require payment or credits.

faq.question: Can it show private dashboards or cloud folders?
faq.answer: The documented workflows support authorized dashboard connections and selected cloud folders. Prefer delegated consent or narrow service accounts; assess hosted password, MFA-seed and cookie storage before use.

faq.question: How does it verify publication?
faq.answer: It checks Player acknowledgments and inspects fresh screenshots. Pending reviews and queued commands are not completed publication, and a still image does not prove continuous playback.
